T: Bangkok. A brother to avenge. Glass on the ropes.
D: After Tong Po cripples his brother in a Bangkok ring, Kurt Sloane learns Muay Thai from a hermit master to fight him the ancient way.
P: Serve the crying tiger beef when Kurt steps into the ring with Tong Po.
S: Tong Po's crying tiger beef with jaew
Grilled steak sliced with a tangy chilli jaew. Tong Po kicks the concrete pillar.

Rub the steak with the soy, oyster sauce and half the sugar and leave for 15 minutes. Toast the rice in a dry pan until deep golden, then grind it to a coarse powder. For the jaew, mix the fish sauce, juice of 2 limes, the rest of the sugar, chilli flakes, shallots and a spoon of the ground rice. Grill the steak over high heat until charred outside and pink inside, then rest it for 5 minutes. Slice thinly, scatter with herbs and the rest of the rice powder, and serve with lettuce cups, lime wedges and the jaew.
Kurt kicks the banana tree down.

Peel off the tough outer layers of the blossom, slice the pale heart very thinly and drop it into water with the juice of a lime. Toast the coconut in a dry pan until golden. Whisk the chilli jam, fish sauce, sugar, coconut cream and the juice of the other lime. Drain the blossom well and toss with the prawns, dressing and herbs. Pile onto a plate and finish with the peanuts and toasted coconut.
M: Pedicab pad kra pao with a crisp fried egg
Holy basil chicken stir-fry over rice with a crisp fried egg. Now you drive me in Pedicab.

Rinse the rice and cook it with 3 cups of water, covered, then rest it off the heat. Pound the garlic and chillies to a rough paste. Fry the paste in the oil in a smoking wok for 30 seconds, add the pork and stir-fry until browned and catching. Add the oyster, fish and soy sauces and the sugar, toss, then wilt in the basil. Fry the eggs in hot oil, spooning it over until the edges are crisp and the yolks still soft, and serve on the rice and pork.
2 tbsp vegetable oil, plus extra for the eggs@Pantry
2 cup holy basil or Thai basil leaves@Produce
White warrior green curry of chicken
Green curry of chicken in coconut milk with rice. The crowd chants Nack Suk Cao.

Put the rice on to cook. Boil the coconut cream in a wok until it splits and the oil shows, then fry the curry paste in it until fragrant. Add the chicken and stir to coat, then add the coconut milk, eggplant and lime leaves and simmer until the chicken is cooked. Season with the fish sauce and sugar, stir in the basil and top with the chilli. Serve with the rice.
6 Thai eggplants, quartered (or 1 small eggplant, diced)@Produce
W: Mango sticky rice with smashed palm sugar glass
Hemp rope, resin and broken glass.

Drain the rice and steam it in a lined steamer until tender and sticky. Meanwhile warm 300ml coconut milk with the 100g sugar and the salt, pour most of it over the hot rice, cover and leave to soak in. Melt the 150g sugar in a dry pan until amber, pour thinly onto baking paper, scatter with sesame and leave to set hard, then smash into shards. Simmer the rest of the coconut milk with the cornflour until thick for the topping. Serve the rice with sliced mango, the thick coconut and shards of glass stuck in the top.
100g caster sugar, plus 150g for the glass@Pantry
K: Mekhong bucket with lime and soda
Thai whisky with lime and soda in a bucket. Xian gets Kurt drunk before the bar fight.
Squeeze the lime wedges into a small ice bucket or large jug and drop them in. Fill with ice, pour in the Mekhong and Red Bull and top with soda. Stir and serve with a straw each.
